sections.name: File setup
sections.title: All backend settings with placeholder values
sections.what: Lists every backend setting in groups, with placeholder values such as a fake API key and a placeholder secret key. Nothing in this file runs. It only documents which settings exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: so a developer can see what to configure before running the app.
sections.watch_out: Copying this file unchanged would turn on debug mode and leave a placeholder secret key in place.

summary: A template listing the backend's settings with placeholder values, meant to be copied and filled in for a real environment.
purpose: To show which settings exist, what form they take, and which placeholder values must be replaced before use.
why: Likely reason: the placeholder wording and the example file name show it is a starting point, not a live configuration. Reason not stated in the code.
how: The file groups settings into the app itself, the API server, the database and cache, AI service keys, web research, session limits, Excel export, security and logging. A developer copies it into a real settings file and replaces the placeholders. How the app reads those values is not in the packet.
inputs: No inputs. A developer reads it as a template, and the copied settings file is what the app would read, which is not shown in the packet.
outputs: No program output. The values are placeholders.
risks: DEBUG and API_RELOAD are on, and the SECRET_KEY placeholder asks for a change. If the copy is used unchanged in production, debug details could be exposed and the secret key would be guessable. The CORS_ORIGINS setting, and the research and session limits, are not read by any file in the packet, so changing them may do nothing.
debug: If the app does not match this template, first check whether a real settings file exists and what values it holds. Check the settings loader in the backend, which is not in the packet. For browser access errors, check the origins fixed in backend/main.py, which may override this file. The database and cache URLs are not used by the code shown, since sessions live in memory.
